title: Proper/open interchange and its base-change and composition equations
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. Use $D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, the bounded-below derived category of constant-coefficient module sheaves on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], derived direct images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and exact extension by zero along open immersions [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. For a commutative square
$$\begin{array}{ccc} A&\xrightarrow{k}&B\\ r\downarrow&&\downarrow p\\ C&\xrightarrow{i}&D\end{array}$$
with $p,r$ proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and $k,i$ open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion], there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$\gamma_Q:i_!Rr_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*k_!.$$
No cartesian hypothesis is imposed. Its normalization on a K-injective representative $J$ of $K\in D^+(A_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ is the morphism represented by $i_!r_*J\cong p_*k_!J\to p_*I$, where $k_!J\to I$ is a K-injective resolution [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions]; the first identification is the canonical proper/open identification of sheaves. When $A=C$, $r=\mathrm{id}$, $k=j_1$, $i=j_2$ and $p=u$ with $uj_1=j_2$, this map equals $\alpha_u$ of [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison].
For vertically stacked squares $Q_1,Q_2$ of this kind, with middle open $i_1$, bottom open $i_2$, left proper maps $r_1,r_2$, and right proper maps $p_1,p_2$, the equation is
$$\gamma_{Q_2Q_1}=(Rp_{2,*}\gamma_{Q_1})\circ(\gamma_{Q_2}Rr_{1,*}):i_{2!}Rr_{2,*}Rr_{1,*}\to Rp_{2,*}Rp_{1,*}k_{1!}.$$
For horizontally adjacent squares with left vertical $r$, middle vertical $p$, right vertical $q$, top opens $k,l$ and bottom opens $i,j$, the equation is
$$\gamma_{Q_2Q_1}=(\gamma_{Q_2}k_!)\circ(j_!\gamma_{Q_1}):j_!i_!Rr_*\to Rq_*l_!k_!,$$
All equations insert the canonical composition isomorphisms of direct images and extension by zero; squares whose two vertical maps are identities give identity comparisons, and squares whose two horizontal maps are identities give the identity on derived direct image.
Finally, let $b:D_1\to D$ be any morphism, let $Q_1$ be the base change of $Q$ by $b$, and write $a:B_1\to B$, $c:C_1\to C$, $d:A_1\to A$ for projections. Let $\beta_i:b^{-1}i_!\cong i_{1!}c^{-1}$ and $\beta_k:a^{-1}k_!\cong k_{1!}d^{-1}$ be the extension-by-zero base-change maps [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change], and let $\operatorname{Ex}_r:c^{-1}Rr_*\to Rr_{1,*}d^{-1}$ and $\operatorname{Ex}_p:b^{-1}Rp_*\to Rp_{1,*}a^{-1}$ be the module exchange maps [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients]. Then
$$ (Rp_{1,*}\beta_k)\circ(\operatorname{Ex}_p k_!)\circ(b^{-1}\gamma_Q)
=(\gamma_{Q_1}d^{-1})\circ(i_{1!}\operatorname{Ex}_r)\circ(\beta_iRr_*). $$ Base changes here are formed by fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product].

proof.text: Construct the ordinary natural isomorphism delta using the proper and open specialization isomorphisms and the composition isomorphisms of [lem-cbc-proper-support-sheaf-composition]. Its two factorizations into the common ordinary direct image give exactly the stated ordinary normalization.

For a fixed square, [lem-cbc-open-extended-injective-proper-acyclic] says that k! sends injectives to p*-right-acyclic objects. Convert positive homology vanishing through homologyRightDerivedFunctorPlusObjSingleFunctorIso. The already proved generic source theorem [src-right-derived-functor-plus-base-change-of-right-acyclic] makes rightDerivedFunctorPlusBaseChange(delta.hom) an isomorphism. Define gamma to be asIso of this canonical map. Its source-library factorization equation, expanded through the homotopy-composition factors, gives the full unit normalization for every J.

For vertical identities, the ordinary normalization and monicity of the open comparison give delta followed by the direct-image identity isomorphism equal to open extension of the other identity isomorphism. Apply rightDerived_ext and the unit normalizations of the derived direct-image identity isomorphisms to deduce the derived identity. For horizontal identities, identify open extension along the identity using the specified adjunction isomorphism. Its hom equals the open inclusion followed by lowerStarId, by the adjunction triangle equations. The ordinary normalization then gives the ordinary identity, and rightDerived_ext together with exact-functor localization factors gives the displayed derived identity. These are formal calculations in the delivered private helpers.

For vertical pasting first prove the ordinary equation by including both paths in their common direct image. Naturality of the inclusions and lowerStarComp_assoc' identify both composites; the inclusion is monic. To lift this equality, use [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-preserves-injectives] to show the composite derived direct images, with rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompUnit, are the right derived functor of the composite. Whisker by the final exact open extension and apply rightDerived_ext. The factorization equations for each canonical base-change map and for rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompIso' reduce the desired equality to the ordinary equation. Naturality moves the factorization isomorphisms and units through the comparison, and the isomorphism cancellation at the end gives exactly the stated compositor orientation. No further geometric or acyclic-complex lemma is needed for this formal step.
